svg.text: solid = flow (join = all) · dashed red = bounded loop · dotted = escalate · white = agent · grey = tool · amber = review · thick red border = human gate

rect.title: Find and register every source that can ground the film — brief, product evidence (prototype, demo recording, spec), brand authority, prior versions and feedback — with an evidence tag, without inventing any.
Hash every local source, detect context gaps (missing brief, product evidence, brand authority, control documents, blocking questions), and freeze the immutable inputs once they are sufficient.
State the film's objective as an observable target, name the audience and the review lenses, set the runtime cap and success criteria, and agree the quality bar (evaluation.md) with Wei.
Establish product truth from the evidence — capabilities, required interactions, demo scenarios, the engineers' terminology, prohibited terms and the only claims the film may make — and lock it.
Propose at least three distinct concept directions with different anchors, each with a structure, strengths and named risks.
Compare the concepts against the objective and success criteria, recommend one, record why the others were rejected, and complete creative.md for Wei's decision.
Write the narration as chapters and units, each unit tagged with the verified claims and product terms it relies on, within the runtime cap.
Turn the script into beats with one communication objective each, progressive disclosure, source-locked visuals, and a full specification for every seam, plus a shot list.

Define the visual language as tokens — palette, approved text pairs, type families and roles, layout and safe areas, motion vocabulary, supplied brand assets, prohibited patterns — plus the technical production spec, and lock both.

Plan every asset the storyboard needs — its role, source type (supplied, captured, generated or rendered), rights, spec and a specific subject — so production is never blocked and nothing is invented.
Produce every planned asset (fan-out over the plan), each at spec and with provenance (source, prompt or capture log, model, hash).
Produce one continuous, identity-consistent narration stem with measured unit timings, plus the audio specification. Never attenuate speech; human listening remains a separate sign-off.
Build each beat as a scene cued to the measured narration — progressive disclosure, one message per frame, purposeful motion — and export the text-layer manifest that the audits read.
Assemble the master (scenes, voice, music bed with look-ahead ducking, captions, loudness normalisation) and the stems, silent master and caption sidecar.
Measure the master itself — format, sync, duration, loudness, silence, black frames, captions — against production.md and the defaults.
An independent critic judges the rendered film through Wei's five lenses and the craft rubric — hook, clarity, one message per frame, motion purpose, transitions, emotional arc, polish.
Trace everything drawn to design.md — palette tokens, approved text pairs, type families, logo integrity, prohibited patterns — and judge cross-scene consistency.
Verify that every text is large enough, has enough contrast, is on screen long enough, sits inside the safe areas and never ghosts; that captions are speech-locked; and that nothing flashes.
Check narration and on-screen text against product truth — terminology, prohibited terms, verified claims — and confirm no product UI was invented and the walkthrough goes deep enough.
Measure speaking rate, runtime against the cap and reading time per beat, and judge narrative clarity, audience relevance and scene-to-scene connection.

Turn every critique and every piece of human feedback into structured defects (severity, dimension, evidence, traced node, smallest fix, acceptance check), then gate the version pass / rework / blocked.
Route each blocking defect to the node that produced it, invalidate only those nodes and their dependents, and snapshot hashes for the before/after comparison.
Recompute the release conditions from disk (gate, defects, reviewed master hash, deliverables, ledger), prepare the release summary, and ask Wei for the release decision.
Package every deliverable with its evidence, hash every file into a manifest, zip it and verify the zip against the manifest.

Capture what this production taught — failures, corrections, approvals, outcomes — separate project-specific lessons from reusable ones, update the project memory, and propose (never apply) rule-base changes.
